gitobj.description: one git object — its entity id IS its SHA-1 object id, so writing the same object twice writes one row

type.description: the word in the object's own header

size.description: the body's length in bytes — the number in that same header

blob.description: where an object's bytes are: their address in the @yaks/blob store

sha.description: the SHA-256 of the bytes — for a git blob it is the app file's own address, never a re-encoded copy

tree_entry.description: a tree holds a child under a name — the walk a pack's reachability needs

name.description: the name this child answers to in this tree; the same tree is a child of many trees under different names, which is why the name is on the link

mode.description: the mode as the tree body spells it: 100644 a file, 40000 a directory

parent.description: this commit follows that one — `ord` on the edge carries parent order

compat.description: git's compat oid: the same object's SHA-256 name, keyed off its SHA-1 one, so either id resolves (git's own hash-function transition, as key rows)

ref.description: where one branch of one repository stands — one row per repository and branch name, so moving a branch patches the row that was there

app.description: the entity the repository belongs to; its branches die with it

commit.description: the commit object the branch points at

target.description: symbolic target full ref name, absent for direct refs

oid.description: raw Git object id; annotated tags need not point directly to commits

present.description: false when a previously observed host ref has been deleted

repository.description: A local Git object database, identified by its canonical common Git directory.

origin.description: where it is published — the remote it was cloned from or pushes to

worktree.description: A local checkout. Identity is repository plus canonical checkout root, not branch or HEAD.

head.description: HEAD object id; absent for unborn HEAD

branch.description: shared ref entity HEAD is attached to; absent for detached HEAD

managed.description: created by this integration, never implies automatic cleanup

checkout.description: Durable host checkout creation intent; ready only after Git succeeds. Failed requests retain their error for retry.

requested.description: original base expression, while base is the pinned commit oid

target.description: the work this commit is about

message.description: the whole commit message, not its first line

commit.description: a landed commit, attached to the work it is about: the sha IS its eid, so recording the same commit twice is one entity

sha.description: the sha it was true at

symbol.description: the symbol it names, when it names one

anchor.description: a promise about source: the paths and sha a document was written against, so freshness is re-derived from git rather than stored

land.title: Land this branch
land.description: Land the branch the caller is standing on. Fast-forwards it into the base — the branch the shared checkout holds — and pushes if the base has an upstream. If the base moved, rebases onto it and returns WITHOUT merging, printing what it pulled in, so the caller can re-gate and land again; that is a refusal, because nothing landed. Refuses a landing whose files carry content no commit on the branch wrote unless allow-revert names them. Runs no gate and reads no graph: every coordinate comes from git, and the checkout is the one the process running this call stands in.

allow-revert.description: comma-separated files whose rewind is deliberate, landed with a warning
